entries.title: Architecture distinction (intentional, not a mismatch) — paper-synthesis vs OneVision-selection-augment
entries.summary: Two architectures live in this repo, intentionally separate (one per paper): (1) RefinedSummarization v1/v2 = synthesis (3 drafters → 1 Llama-70B refiner that merges); (2) Refine-OneVision-Summary = selection-then-augment (3 drafters → Borda voter → 1 winning draft → SingleDraftVerifier on full paragraphs → Retriever → augmenting refiner; optionally K=3 + winner-as-refiner). User confirmed: there is NO third 'B7 NLI selector' architecture; that was a misremembered design that doesn't exist in any branch.
entries.source: User confirmation 2026-05-07; verified against current paper main.tex §3 and Refine-OneVision-Summary src/agents/voter.py

entries.title: Refine-OneVision-Summary unit test suite
Re-run the 5 stalled long papers under OneVision v2 with timeout protection

config.fix_required: Add asyncio.wait_for timeout to drafter / refiner LLMClient calls (e.g., 600 s per call); set EXPERIMENT_CONCURRENCY=1 to avoid Qwen-72B rate-limit thrashing.

entries.hypothesis: v2 specifically helps long, multi-section papers (more facts to retrieve via iterative refine). Including the 5 killed papers should *strengthen* v2's win over v1 on the n=29 paired comparison.

entries.title: NLI-based selector (replace Borda voter with NLI scorer)

config.design_source: Self-designed (no prior spec exists; user authorised proceeding from scratch).
config.approach_sketch: For each draft, run DeBERTa-v3-base-mnli-fever-anli on every (draft-claim, paper-paragraph) pair. Sum max-entailment per draft. Pick the draft with the highest summed entailment. Implementation lives in a new src/agents/nli_selector.py module that swaps in for src/agents/voter.py.

entries.hypothesis: An NLI classifier scoring each (draft, paper-paragraph) pair gives a more calibrated draft-quality signal than LLM Borda voting, and may pick something other than Qwen 93% of the time (i.e., real per-paper selection). Could shift the voter accuracy from 14/27 = 52% (Qwen-bias) toward higher.

entries.title: Refiner model swap: replace Llama-70B refiner with Qwen-72B (full pipeline, n=29)

config.rationale: Tests whether the L1 'family homogeneity caps refiner ceiling' hypothesis is robust: if Qwen-refiner v1 still loses to B2 Qwen-naive, the ceiling is set by the *single-refiner architecture*, not by the Llama backbone.

entries.hypothesis: Qwen-refined v1 will edge above Llama-refined v1 by ~+0.05–0.10 F1 (closing some of the family-homogeneity gap), but will still lose to B2 Qwen-naive — confirming that the merging architecture is the bottleneck even with the strongest backbone.

entries.title: Recompute E15 voter audit + decompose the +0.106 OneVision-vs-B6 contrast

config.deliverable: A script that reports, per paper: (winning agent, OneVision F1, B2 F1, B6 F1, Δ(OneVision − B6) decomposition into [model-swap component] + [augmenter component])

entries.hypothesis: The augmenter degradation component will be larger on papers where Qwen draft was already good, smaller on papers where Qwen draft missed facts. Identifies which papers OneVision actually helps vs which it just rides Qwen's coattails on.

entries.title: Decompose L9 — compute Δ(B2 − B6) on n=29 paired

config.deliverable: Compute paired (B2 Qwen-72B-naive − B6 Llama-70B-v2-prompt) on the n=29 sample under both judges. This is the 'pure backbone-swap' contrast (Qwen vs Llama, same prompt). Then: Δ(OneVision − B6) − Δ(B2 − B6) = isolated augmenter effect.

entries.hypothesis: Δ(B2 − B6) ≈ +0.16 strict / +0.17 deberta. If true, the OneVision +0.106 vs B6 contrast decomposes cleanly into 'voter picks Qwen base instead of Llama base' (most of it) + 'augmenter degrades by ~0.06'. Validates L9 numerically.
